title: Multiple matching – AI in our daily lives

atoms.text: You will hear five people talking about AI in their daily lives. First, read the statements. Then listen to the audio file and match each speaker (1 to 5) with one of the statements.
atoms.sound: You will hear five people talking about AI in their daily lives. First reed the statements. Then listen to the audio file and match each speaker with one of the statements.

instruction.sound: speaker 1 <voice voiceLang='en' voice='f5Us_chirp'>Honestly, I think AI has transformed my working routine. It automates repetitive tasks like scheduling or sorting emails, which gives me more time for the creative side of my business. Of course, there are concerns about data use, but for me, the efficiency and productivity gains are simply undeniable. Without these tools, I would probably need to hire extra staff.</voice> speaker 2 <voice voiceLang='en' voice='m3Au_chirp'>In education, AI is a mixed blessing. On one hand, adaptive learning software really helps weaker students by giving them personalized feedback. On the other hand, I see pupils using AI to generate essays without really thinking for themselves. It saves time, sure, but it undermines genuine learning. That’s why we need very clear rules on when and how it can be used.</voice> speaker 3 <voice voiceLang='en' voice='f8_chirp'>What truly worries me is privacy. Many AI applications rely on huge amounts of personal data — conversations, photos, even medical records. Once such data is collected, you never know how securely it’s stored or who has access to it. Efficiency is nice, but the risk of abuse is far too great. For me, strict regulations and transparency are absolutely necessary.</voice> speaker 4 <voice voiceLang='en' voice='m8_chirp'>AI is not just some abstract concept for me — it has cost me my job. Machines powered by AI now perform tasks I used to do on the production line, only faster and without breaks. Of course, companies call this “progress,” but for workers like me, it feels more like being replaced. I’m not against technology, but I want fair opportunities to retrain and find new work.</voice> speaker 5 <voice voiceLang='en' voice='f2Us_chirp'>I can’t imagine my life without AI anymore. It helps me navigate the city, learn languages, even recommend films I enjoy. It’s like having a personal assistant who knows me really well. I understand some people are worried, but to me the benefits far outweigh the drawbacks. Honestly, it makes everyday life much easier and more fun.</voice>
